efficacy.confidence_note: Abstracts and registry read. Seletalisib (NCT02610543, terminated, n=27): ESSDAI −2.59 vs placebo, 95% CI −7.30 to 2.11, P=0.266; saliva and tear flow unchanged. Leniolisib (NCT02775916, n=29): ESSPRI net −0.69 (95% CI −3.34 to 1.94); ESSDAI net +0.51 (favoured placebo).
efficacy.judgement: Scored unsettled, not contra: seletalisib was terminated at 36% power with a favourable trend, and leniolisib's 29-patient CIs span both benefit and harm. A stricter reader could call the two null primaries plus unchanged saliva flow (the mouse's own functional readout) contra. Leniolisib was not dosed in the mouse. Co-primary ruling: scored as the authors call the trial; they report a trend toward improvement and do not call it a failure, so it stays unsettled. Leniolisib (not dosed in the mouse) gave the same inconclusive result, so its trial stays in patient_trials and no track is split. Parsaclisib's NCT03627065 is scored on its own NOD-mouse track.
efficacy.note: Mice predicted fewer gland infiltrates and better saliva flow. Seletalisib's co-primaries were safety and week-12 ESSDAI: ESSDAI −2.59 vs placebo (P=0.266) in a trial stopped at 36% power, which the authors call a trend, not a failure; leniolisib's trial was also inconclusive.
efficacy.quote: Enrolment challenges led to early study termination with loss of statistical power (36% vs 80% planned).

patient_trials.quote: a trend for improvement in ESSDAI and ESSPRI [difference vs placebo: -2.59 (95% CI: -7.30, 2.11; P=0.266) and -1.55 (95% CI: -3.39, 0.28), respectively] was observed at week 12.

Passing tolerability ruling: the mouse claim is a safety prediction, contradicted by excess serious AEs and AE withdrawals in Sjögren's patients; diarrhoea and weight-related harm were within the mouse's reach.
